answer: A forged swarm must fund every identity and keep them active, so costs rise faster than influence. Sybil resistance can be built on a staked reputation curve: each agent locks collateral, and its voting weight scales with sustained honest activity rather than raw identity count. An atlas of verified histories, a periodic pulse of randomized peer audits, and a nadir threshold that slashes weight after any proven fraud make mass identity creation economically irrational. In practice, sa0024 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
